% Title: An exact all-cutoff obstruction to PAH-v2 full-cylinder sup generator convergence
% Claim: C6-SPACETIME-SIGNATURE
% Version: v1.0 -- first issued 2026-09-12; this version issued 2026-09-12
% Status: scoped exact negative result R-572; no host tier action
% Revision history: v1.0 (2026-09-12) first gate-level synthesis.

\section*{1. Purpose and scope}
This note addresses exactly PAH-V2-GD-001, not a repaired or weaker problem.
The immutable preregistration is
\url{strategy/pa-hyp/PAH-v2-GD-001-prereg-v1.json}, with SHA-256
\begin{verbatim}
a3079a674ef328134ed28aafc82d9baa7a16068beb7040410a1a7facca4c3390
\end{verbatim}
The adopted comparison bundle remains
\begin{verbatim}
1d6fa47f5351d74f05bed3aba5b1e229a827644d4c6ef5d7dd73c117adee95b6
\end{verbatim}
The separate execution supplement records the user's authorization and fixed
probe before the implementation checks. Historical setting-only metadata is
preserved. The source PAH-001-v1 functional and PAH-001-v2-r2 labelled state,
rates and roots are unchanged; every source hash is in the result certificate.

At fixed parameters and fixed lattice/exhaustion indices $h,N$, write
$I_{r,s}f=f\circ p_{s,r}$. For a single fixed $r_0,f_0$ in the full finite
invariant algebra, the target asks whether
\[
 \lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_{s>r\ge R}
 \|L_s I_{r_0,s}f_0-I_{r,s}L_r I_{r_0,r}f_0\|_\infty=0. \tag{1}
\]
The norm ranges over every fine counting tuple, not typical Gibbs states.
The time is the original external Markov time, without acceleration or a
factor of one half in the generator. The original order is local-state cutoff
$r$, lattice $h$, exhaustion $N$, then the inherited later stages. Only the
first stage is tested; there is no interchange or diagonal limit.

For the counterexample fix $h=N=r_0=0$, $q_0=m_0=R_0=1$, $\epsilon=1$,
and $\beta=\nu=\lambda_s=\eta_6=\kappa_s=\kappa_D=\kappa_g=g=1$,
$m^2=\lambda_4=0$. These are admitted inserted parameters, not fitted outputs.
The literal displayed rates have no additional coefficient. Any separately
referenced inserted rate scale is held at unity. The adopted box has side two,
four vertices, four stored oriented edges and its single square face, with
anchors $O=(0,0)$ and $C=(1,0)$. This is an existing combinatorial carrier,
not a new physical dimension or volume.

\section*{2. Full-source reduction, including all root families}
Put $M_r=2^r$. The remaining prescribed cutoffs are the primorial $K_r$,
$M_{\psi,r}=4^r$, $R_{\max,r}=2^r$ and $Q_r=2^r$. At $\epsilon=1$,
\[
 s_v=1+j_v(1-1)/M_r=1
\]
for every aperture label. Crucially, the approved state space still counts
all $j_v\in\{0,\ldots,M_r\}$ as distinct. These labels are not quotiented.

The parent functional depends on $j$ only through $s$. In its onsite terms,
$s=1$ removes every $j$; the aperture edge energy is zero; $J_e=1$ and
$J_p=1$, so the covariant matter and plaquette terms also have no $j$.
An AP move changes no occupation, phase or link coordinate. Therefore every
valid AP move has exactly $\Delta F=0$, mobility
$(s_{\rm before}s_{\rm after})^{\nu/2}=1$, and rate
\[
 c_{\rm AP}=1\exp(-\beta\,0/2)=1. \tag{2}
\]
This argument is valid for all other finite coordinates, not only the witness.
All finite rates exist: the finite counting space, $\epsilon>0$ and finite
parameters make every displayed functional term and rate finite.

PH changes phase only; LK changes a link only; TR changes occupation only.
Consequently they preserve every aperture coordinate and every cutoff
pullback of an aperture-only observable. Their increments are separately zero
before multiplication by their finite rates. AP at a vertex other than $O$
also has zero increment. These are exact zero contributions in the complete
labelled sums, not deletion, matching, averaging or cancellation of roots.
Both signs are retained, including the separate duplicate labels at $K=2$.
At $j_O=0$ the negative AP move is invalid; at $j_O=M_r$ the positive one is
invalid. The source omits these moves, without wrapping or reflection.

\section*{3. All-index formula and fixed-data counterexample}
Fix once and for all $f_0=\mathbf1_{\{j_O=0\}}$ at $r_0=0$.
It is gauge invariant because gauge transformations leave $j$ fixed, and
anchor invariant because the allowed automorphisms fix $O$.
It has full-state sup norm one. R-571 gives, at the same $h,N$,
$j_O\mapsto\lfloor j_O/2^{s-r}\rfloor$. Thus for every $r\ge0$,
\[
 f_r=I_{0,r}f_0=\mathbf1_{\{j_O<M_r\}}.
\]
This is one fixed cylinder observable, not a cutoff-dependent selection.
The complete generator, by (2) and the individual zero increments above, is
\[
 L_r f_r(x)=\mathbf1_{\{j_O=M_r\}}-
                  \mathbf1_{\{j_O=M_r-1\}}. \tag{3}
\]
Indeed the only downward jump across the indicator discontinuity starts at
$M_r$, and the only upward jump across it starts at $M_r-1$.
The signs in (3) are respectively positive and negative. This also proves the
endpoint case $M_r=1$: the two states have generator values $-1,+1$.

For arbitrary $s>r\ge0$, set $D=2^{s-r}\ge2$, so $M_s=DM_r$.
For every fine tuple, the pullback of the positive indicator in (3) is
$\mathbf1_{\{j_O=M_s\}}$. The pullback of the negative indicator is
$\mathbf1_{\{M_s-D\le j_O<M_s\}}$. Subtracting the complete coarse
generator from the fine generator gives the exact all-state identity
\[
 \boxed{\displaystyle
  (L_s I_{r,s}f_r-I_{r,s}L_r f_r)(x)
  =\mathbf1_{\{M_s-D\le j_O<M_s-1\}}.} \tag{4}
\]
There is no half factor, volume factor, density correction or norm change.
The band in (4) is nonempty because $D\ge2$; it has $D-1$ integer labels.
For any such label a valid full state exists: put all occupation $Q_s=2^s$
at $O$, zero occupation elsewhere, and choose any admitted phase/link labels.
This is valid since $2^s\le4^s$. Hence on the full fine counting space
\[
 \|L_s I_{r,s}f_r-I_{r,s}L_r f_r\|_\infty=1
 \quad\text{for every }s>r\ge0. \tag{5}
\]

\begin{theorem}
The universal full-invariant-cylinder sup-norm Cauchy statement (1) is false
for the exact adopted PAH-v2 model and comparison at its allowed
$\epsilon=1$ boundary. Its GD-001 verdict is DISPROVED.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Fix the parameters, carrier and observable specified above and $\eta_0=1$.
For every integer tail threshold $R\ge0$, choose $r=R$, $s=r+1$ and
$j_O=2^{r+1}-2$. Set all other $j$ and every phase/link label to zero and
put $\ell_O=Q_s$, all other occupations zero. This is an admitted full tuple
at every such cutoff. Formula (4) gives defect one there. Thus there cannot
be a tail on which all defects are strictly below $\eta_0$. Formula (5)
proves the stronger all-pair norm identity. No finite-table extrapolation
enters the argument.
\end{proof}

\section*{4. Independent formulation and kernel bridge}
An independent row formulation takes the AP generator on
$\{0,\ldots,M\}$ with off-diagonal entries one between adjacent integers
and diagonal equal to minus the number of valid neighbors. Applying this
matrix to the vector $(1,\ldots,1,0)$ gives zero except at its last two
coordinates, which are $-1,+1$. Every other full root has zero aperture
increment. Pulling back the last two coordinate indicators by integer division
gives exactly the two intervals used in (4). This independently audits sign,
row sums, endpoint domain and the absence of a multiplicity factor.

The primary executable uses the pinned full source move enumerator and the
composed source maps, plus a symbolic expansion of every parent functional
term with generic amplitudes and phase cosines. The independent executable
imports neither primary nor either source backend: it builds simultaneous
coordinate moves, direct all-pair floors and row actions separately. Fixed
fixtures check every $j_O$ at $(r,s)=(0,1),(1,2),(1,3),(2,3)$, including
nonzero phase/link labels. These fixtures test the implementations of the
general proof; they are not its universal evidence.

\url{verification/lean/Tect/PahV2GeneratorDefect.lean} formalizes five
parameterized statements under pinned Lean 4.32.1: endpoint generator,
fixed-base pullback, the complete adjacent defect for every $M\ge1$, its
witness at $2M-2$, and an unbounded-tail witness for every $R$ with $M=2^R$.
The encoded AP definition explicitly omits invalid endpoint moves. The
model-to-AP reduction, gauge/anchor invariance and full-state occupation
admissibility are the written bridge above, not fully formalized PAH data.
The nonadjacent formula (4) is analytic; the Lean adjacent theorem already
suffices for the exact negation of (1). No unproved escape is used.

Independent implementation and hostile review were authored within this same
task, not by an external referee. External review of (2)--(4), the hidden-label
domain and the fixed-data quantifiers is explicitly invited.

\section*{5. Devil's-advocate review and applicability}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{DISMISSED: equal displayed apertures identify the states.}
The approved v2 integer counting definition explicitly retains $j$ at
$\epsilon=1$. Quotienting it would change the model and the observable class.
\item \textbf{DISMISSED: an omitted root cancels the defect.}
All PH/TR/LK increments, and AP increments away from $O$, vanish individually.
Both signed AP moves at $O$ are included exactly when valid.
\item \textbf{DISMISSED: the factor is one half or the sign is reversed.}
The source generator has no half; only $B$ has $\sqrt{c/2}$. The definition
is fine minus coarse. At the adjacent witness the two values are $0,-1$.
\item \textbf{DISMISSED: the observable changes with the cutoff.}
It is always the same $f_0$ pulled back from $r_0=0$. Only the witness state
and the two comparison indices vary, as allowed by the exact negation.
\item \textbf{DISMISSED: this is only a small-cutoff artifact.}
The proof covers every integer $s>r\ge0$; the kernel covers every adjacent
pair through $M=2^r$, including an explicit witness beyond each threshold.
\item \textbf{UPHELD boundary: sup failure need not be Gibbs-$L^2$ failure.}
No Gibbs weight or weak convergence was evaluated. This result cannot be
used to decide either or a smaller limiting-generator domain.
\item \textbf{UPHELD boundary: one parameter boundary is not all parameters.}
The counterexample disproves the universal target, not every fixed
$0<\epsilon<1$ case or the finite consistency of R-570/R-571.
\end{itemize}

The bounded literature/legacy search and hypothesis crosswalk are in the
execution supplement. The exact parent definitions supply (2); R-571 supplies
the finite floor pullbacks and invariant algebra only. Earlier strip,
free-vertex and radial results have different scopes and are not imported.
No external theorem or novelty priority is claimed. Units in (3)--(5) are
observable per unchanged external Markov time; the zero-tolerance tests are
integer/symbolic equalities, not floating approximations.

\section*{6. Result footer and one next question}
\begin{description}
\item[Result ID] R-572; exploration EXP-001739.
\item[Precise statement] Equations (4)--(5) on the allowed $\epsilon=1$
boundary disprove the exact universal GD-001 target with one fixed $f_0$.
\item[Scope] Fixed adopted four-vertex open carrier; arbitrary state cutoff
pairs; full fine counting sup norm; original external Markov time.
\item[Dependencies] Immutable PAH-v1 functional, PAH-v2-r2 signed counting
definitions, and R-571 adopted comparison; all pins in the certificate.
\item[Evidence grade] ANALYTIC, EXACT, EXECUTED; partial parameterized Lean.
\item[Reproduction command] See the command below and result certificate.
\item[Expected output] All four verification lanes PASS; GD-001 DISPROVED.
\item[Falsification gate] A source-compatible nonzero contribution omitted
from (3), an invalid fixed witness, or a failed floor identity would refute
this negative result and require append-only correction.
\item[Tier before / after] Host C6 remains T1; no T-054 gate change. The
negative result is exact only in its declared model/route scope.
\item[No-overclaim statement] No physical Pre-A, spacetime, QFT, gravity,
continuum, common causal cone, Yang--Mills, mass gap or TOE conclusion.
No infinite dynamics, alternative-domain no-go or Gibbs-$L^2$ verdict.
\item[Next required action] Before any replacement convergence target, ask
one question: what source-authorized observable domain and topology, if any,
should replace the refuted full-cylinder sup generator target while keeping
this model and time? No such replacement is selected or tested here.
\end{description}
Reenter this exact target only for a source/domain error or an exact attack
on (2)--(4); do not repeat larger finite tables. A proposed weaker target
requires separate authorization and must retain this negative record.
